 The Honourable Sri Justice V Srinivas

sentences.text:
The Court made the following:
Assailing the judgment dated 28.10.2010 in Crl.A.No.282 of 2008 on the file of the Court of learned III Additional Sessions Judge, Kakinada, confirming the conviction and sentence passed against the petitioner/accused No.3 by the judgment dated 01.09.2008 in C.C.No.3 of 2001 on the file of the Court of learned II Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Kakinada, for the offences under section 468, 469 and 420 of Indian Penal Code (hereinafter referred to as "IPC"), the petitioner/accused No.3 filed the present criminal revision case under Section 397 r/w.401 of the Criminal Procedure Code, 1973.
2.
The revision case was admitted on 02.11.2010 and the sentence of imprisonment imposed against the petitioner was suspended, vide orders in Crl.R.C.M.P.No.3002 of 2010.

3. The shorn of necessary facts are that:
i).
Accused No.1 started Tutorial College during the year, 1997 in the name and style of Sarvani Institute in D.No.36-24-3 from L.K.G. to Degree Class.
Accused Nos.2 to 7 are close associates of accused No.1.
All the accused resorted to the business of preparing and supplying fake educational qualification certificates to the needy persons for monetary gain and they are men of deceitful characters.

ii). P.W.1, who is son of P.W.1, studied in V.T. High School, Rajahmundry having been admitted in VIII Class in the said school on 22.07.1995 and he appeared for M.D.Noori Ahmed vs The State Of A.P. on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6476099/
1

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: S.S.C. examination during March, 1998 as a regular candidate from the said school with Roll No.0172319.
He failed in the said examination and he was also supplied with said failed marks list issued by the S.S.C. Board.

iii). Then P.W.2 admitted P.W.1 in the said Tutorial College of accused No.1 during January, 1998 and at that time, accused No.1 demanded Rs.5,000/- on the assurance of 'pass guarantee', otherwise, he would refund the amount.

However, P.W.1 failed in the said examination, when P.W.2 questioned accused No.1 as to why P.W.1 failed inspite of assurance, accused No.1 misrepresented him that mistake had taken place in S.S.C. Board Office, he verified the results and he would receive revised pass certificate with marks obtained by P.W.1 through V.T. High School.
iv).

On 29.08.1998, a courier cover was received in V.T. High School with one S.S.C.
certificate in the name of P.W.1 with Roll No.0172319 by P.W.3-Junior Assistant in V.T. High School and he placed the same before P.W.4-Head Master.

They noticed discrepancies in the said certificate with regard to the date of birth, father's name and marks secured since they earlier received another marks list and also difference in the total and some other grounds and thus suspected the genuineness of the said certificate.

Thereby, P.W.4 referred the said certificate to the Commissioner for Government Examinations with a letter dated 31.08.1998 for verification and confirmation of the genuineness of the said certificate.
v). During verification of the said certificate in the Office of Director of Government Examinations, A.P., Hyderabad, it was found that it is a bogus certificate and it was not issued by them.

On a compliant received from P.W.12-Director of Government Examinations, dated 29.08.2000, the Director and Inspector General of Police,
Hyderabad, registered a case in Cr.No.27 of 2000 of C.I.D. Police Station, Hyderabad and it was entrusted to P.W.14-Inspector of Police, C.I.D., East Godavari District,
Kakinada for investigation.

v). During investigation, on 25.06.2000, P.W.14 arrested the accused and recorded their confessional statements and seized Exs.P.3 to P.5 fake degree certificates, certain blank provisional forms and marks lists of Andhra University.

4. After completion of investigation, P.W.13-Inspector of Police, C.B.C.I.D., East Godavari at Kakinada laid charge sheet and the same was numbered as C.C.No.3 of 2001 on the file of the Court of learned II Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Kakinada and trial was conducted and found the accused Nos.1 to 4 and 7 guilty of the offences under Section 468, 469, 420 and 120-B of IPC and sentenced them to undergo simple imprisonment of two (2) years each and to pay fine of Rs.1,000/- each, in default to suffer simple imprisonment for one (1) month each, sentenced them to undergo simple imprisonment of one (1) year each and to pay fine of Rs.500/- each, in default to suffer simple imprisonment for one (1) month each, sentenced them to undergo simple imprisonment of one (1) year each and to pay fine of Rs.500/- each, in default to suffer simple imprisonment for one (1) month each

sentences.text: All the sentences imposed against the accused shall run concurrently.
The case against accused Nos.5 and 6 is abated as they died.

5. Aggrieved by the same, the petitioner/accused No.3 preferred an appeal, vide Crl.A.No.282 of 2008, before the Court of learned III Additional Sessions Judge, Kakinada and the same was allowed in part, vide judgment dated 28.10.2010, by setting aside the conviction and sentence passed against the petitioner/accused No.3 for the offence under Section 120-B of IPC, however,
confirmed the conviction and passed by the trial Court for the offences under Section 468, 469 and 420 of IPC.
6.
Against the said judgment of the first Appellate Court, the present criminal revision case was preferred by the petitioner/accused No.3.

7. Heard Sri G.V.S.Mehar Kumar, learned counsel for the petitioner/accused No.3 and Sri S.Dheera Kanishk, learned Special Assistant Public Prosecutor for the respondent-State.
8.

Now the point that arises for determination in this revision is "whether there is any manifest error of law or flagrant miscarriage of justice in the findings recorded by the first Appellate Court?"
9.

Sri G.V.S.Mehar Kumar, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner has not forged, fabricated the certificates and he only the send the cover to the de facto complainant; that the alleged offences are not attracted to the case against the petitioner; that accused No.1 had only created the false, fake certificates and forged the signatures of the officials; that the Courts below ought not to have considered the confession statements of co-accused; that the Trial Court as well Sessions Court failed to appreciate the material on record in a proper perspective and erroneously convicted the petitioner and the same is liable to be set aside.

10. Per contra, Sri S.Dheera Kanishk, learned Special Assistant Public Prosecutor for the respondent submits that the petitioner along with other accused conspired together and supplied fake educational qualification certificates; that the unchallenged evidence of P.Ws.1 and 2 shows that P.W.1 obtained coaching from accused No.1 college, but he failed in the examinations; the other testimonies of prosecution witnesses i.e., P.Ws.3 to 15 categorically established the case against the petitioner and other accused for the said offences; that the prosecution proved the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubt by examining P.Ws.1 to 15 and producing Exs.P.1 to P.16 and that the Courts below right appreciated the material on record and convicted the accused for the said offence.
11. In view of the above rival contentions, this Court perused the material available on record.
The only contention raised by the petitioner is that he was falsely implicated in this case and the prosecution failed to establish the offences alleged against him.
It is not in dispute that petitioner/accused No.3 sent the Ex.P.8 cover to V.T. High School and it contains the handwriting of the petitioner.

3 12.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The testimony of P.Ws.1 and 2 shows that P.W.1 obtained coaching from the tutorials of accused No.1, but he failed in public examination and P.W.2 questioned accused No.1, on which accused No.1 made false representations that some errors had kept in the results announced by S.S.C. Board.

The testimony of P.W.2 also shows that he came to know that the school authorities received 10th class certificate in the name of P.W.1 and having suspected the same, they reported the matter to the Board.

13. The testimony of P.W.3 Junior Assistant and P.W.15 Head Master of V.T. High School shows that P.W.1 appeared for public examination of S.S.C. in the year, 1998 as a regular candidate, but he failed and failed marks certificate and transfer certificate were issued to him.

Subsequently, their school received Ex.P.1 another marks list through courier service without having any courier stamp in Ex.P.8 cover and on suspecting the same, they sent Ex.P.1 to the Commissioner, S.S.C. Board.

The testimony of P.Ws.3 and 15 corroborated the testimony of P.W.5 Deputy Commissioner,
Government Examinations, A.P., Hyderabad.
14.

The testimony of P.W.14 investigating officer categorically shows the investigation done by him and seizure of Exs.P.3 to P.5 fake provisional certificates, marks list and four blank statements of marks lists and one blank provisional certificate under the cover of Ex.P.6 mediators report in the presence of P.Ws.7 and 8.
Even though P.W.7 did not support the prosecution versions, the testimony of P.W.14 is fully corroborated to the testimony of P.W.8.

The testimony of P.W.10 Scientific Officer categorically shows that Ex.P.1 is a fake pass certificate cum marks list and Ex.P.8 courier cover in which Ex.P.1 was sent to V.T. High School contained the handwriting of petitioner/accused No.3.
It is very much evident that petitioner/accused No.3 with knowledge of things assisted accused No.1 in supplying the said certificates to the candidates.

15. Furthermore, the testimony of P.W.14 coupled with P.W.8 and Ex.P.6 mediators report show that some other certificates in the name of two other individuals said to have been issued by Andhra University and some blank certificate/marks list in the name of Andhra University were also seized from the possession of accused No.1 at the time of inspection of his premises.

As per the testimony of P.Ws.6 and 11 foreman and Professor of Andhra University respectively, they verified the genuineness of Exs.P.3 to P.5 and replied that the said certificates are not printed and issued by the Andhra University Press.
The testimony of P.W.11 remained unchallenged.
It is not explained by the petitioner/accused No.3 as to why he sent Ex.P.8 cover to the school.

On the other hand, the testimony of prosecution witnesses clinchingly established the prosecution case against the petitioner/accused No.3.
16.

The trial Court as well Sessions Court categorically held that the testimony of prosecution witnesses clearly goes to show that the prosecution is able to prove the guilt of the petitioner/accused No.3 beyond all reasonable doubt for the said offences.
17. It is settled law

that in view of the concurrent findings on facts by the Trial Court as well Sessions Court, this Court being Revisional Court is not expected to set aside the same without any material of perversity or manifest error in the findings arrived by both the Courts below.
There is no material before this Court to discard the trustworthiness of prosecution witnesses.

M.D.Noori Ahmed vs The State Of A.P. on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6476099/
4 18.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: All these facts go to show that the first Appellate Court rightly came to conclusion that the petitioner/accused No.1 along with other accused committed the said offences and there is no material on record to disbelieve the prosecution case.

Thereby, there is no apparent failure on the part of the Sessions Court in appreciating the evidence on record or to arrive at a conclusion that prosecution proved the guilt of the accused for the said offences.
In these circumstances, this Court is of the considered opinion that there is no perversity or flaw in the findings recorded by the Sessions Court in convicting the accused for the said offences.

19. Having regard to the above discussion, this Court is of the considered opinion that there are no grounds to interfere with the well-articulated judgment of the Sessions Court and thereby, this revision has no merits.
Consequently, the present revision is liable to be dismissed.

20. In the result, the Criminal Revision Case is dismissed confirming the judgment dated 28.10.2010 in Crl.A.No.282 of 2008 on the file of the Court of learned III Additional Sessions Judge,
Kakinada.

The petitioner/accused No.3 is directed to surrender before the Court of learned II Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Kakinada, to serve the sentence imposed, if not, the learned Magistrate concerned shall take steps against the petitioner.
